title: Dedicated capacity prioritization workflow for enterprise tail-latency guarantees
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Workstream to define a repeatable intake + prioritization workflow for enterprise Dedicated capacity requests that require explicit tail-latency guarantees (p99/p99.9). Current intake artefacts focus on throughput and monthly commit sizing; this ticket captures a separate rubric and operational runbook covering: 1) How PMs surface tail-latency requirements during sales handoff, 2) How we translate customer-level latency SLOs into model / GPU class / batching / caching constraints, and 3) The prioritization policy when reserved capacity is scarce (e.g., hybrid burst vs. hard latency SLAs).
proposal: Deliver two artifacts: (A) a scoring rubric that ingests a short preflight questionnaire (latency SLO, traffic shape, max token length, acceptable cost uplift) and outputs recommended GPU family + reserved qps + min-batch and KV cache profile; (B) an ops decision tree used by capacity concierge to accept/decline/modify commitments and offer mitigations (fallback model variants, regional failover, latency-only reserved lanes). Implement initial automation to surface recommendations in the intake UI and as a summary in the SLA proposal PDF.
decision_log: 2026-03-10: PM sync decided to treat tail-latency guarantees as a separate scoring axis from throughput commitments. 2026-03-11: Engineering agreed to expose per-GPU latency curves for standard model families to feed rubric. 2026-03-12: Design approved a compact intake flow that pushes only required burden to sales reps.
acceptance_criteria: A compact preflight questionnaire added to the enterprise intake that captures: p95/p99 targets, traffic spike factor, max prompt+response token length, strictness (soft/hard), region preference

A scoring rubric document that maps questionnaire answers to: recommended GPU family (e.g., A100-80G, H100-80G, L4x2), reserved qps range, suggested min-batch and caching profile, and an estimated cost uplift percentage
An ops runbook with decision tree for 3 outcomes: Approve as-is, Approve with mitigations, Escalate to Architecture Review Board
Prototype integration in intake UI that shows a "Recommended SLA" card and a downloadable SLA proposal draft
Stakeholder signoff from Sales Engineering, Capacity Ops, and Runtime Engineering on the recommended mappings
At least one live customer intake processed through the new workflow (can be a pilot) with post-mortem recorded
tasks: Create preflight questionnaire copy and embed fields into intake form
Collect latency curves and operational constraints from Runtime Engineering for top 4 model families
Design scoring rubric spreadsheet and validation harness (sample inputs + outputs)
Implement UI "Recommended SLA" card prototype in intake tool (read-only initially)
Draft ops runbook and escalate paths for capacity shortages
Pilot the process with two enterprise accounts and capture telemetry and feedback
Iterate rubric thresholds based on pilot latency data and cost impact
risks: Latency curves vary significantly with customer prompt distributions; rubric may under/over-provision if inputs are inaccurate
Customers may request hard p99.9 guarantees that are cost-prohibitive without vendor-specific custom kernels
Misalignment between sales expectation and actual achievable SLOs leading to churn
Operational complexity: enforcing reserved latency lanes may conflict with existing autoscaling policies
